solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mother introduces daughter to adults-only movie

indicators.note: the mother takes the daughter into herself, so one word is set inside the other

parts.note: mama is a familiar word for mother
X was the old British certificate for films restricted to adults

explanation.surface: A mother takes her daughter along to see an X-rated film.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes inside MAMA to give MADMA; X, the old adults-only film rating, finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a famous Australian action film franchise starring Mel Gibson, then Tom Hardy.

clue.text: Audition for suitable bass to accompany a loud US singer

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the words before us are to be taken by their sound

parts.note: meet is an old word for suitable and low describes a bass note, and together they sound like the first part
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: Looks like a casting call for a fitting bass voice to back a loud American vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: MEET LOW, said out loud, gives MEAT LO; A and F (forte) follow. 'Meet' as an adjective meaning fitting is old-fashioned but still in dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage name belongs to the American rock vocalist of Bat Out of Hell fame.

clue.text: Piece of information lawyer has got on corporation

parts.note: a DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer
corporation is a jocular old word for a pot belly, as is tum

explanation.surface: A lawyer has picked up a fact about a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like business but is the old joke word for a large stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single fact or given figure, the singular of data.

clue.text: Supplies best quality hinges

parts.note: A, as in A1 or grade A, stands for top quality
in stamp collecting, hinges and mounts are the small fixings holding stamps on the album page

explanation.surface: Reads like a catalogue line about top-grade door hinges for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hinges' is the stamp collector's word, not a door fitting or a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplies as a noun means quantities or stocks of something, which is what amounts are.

clue.text: At social occasion, rude person dismisses a song and dance

parts.note: a ball is a formal social dance

indicators.note: the lout sends away the single letter named by the word a

parts.note: a yahoo is a boorish lout, from Gulliver's Travels

explanation.surface: At a party, a boor brushes off a performance piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song and dance' looks like the performance at the ball, but it is a fuss; a yahoo is a lout, from Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: A song and dance is a fuss or commotion, and so is a hullabaloo of noisy publicity.

clue.text: Gaffers given position outside? No way, as previously stated

indicators.note: the shortened word goes around the outside of the gaffers
no tells us the following word's abbreviation is taken away

parts.note: to be stationed is to be given a post or position
ST is short for street, a way
gaffer is British slang for a boss or foreman

explanation.surface: Bosses posted outside? Not a chance, as was said earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' signals removal, leaving ATIONED, which goes outside. 'Gaffer' is British slang for the person in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mentioned before in a text is referred to as having been stated earlier.

clue.text: Plain-living sort, loner wandering round US city

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the city
letters that wander roam into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A solitary drifter wanders around an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wandering' scrambles the loner; 'round' puts the jumble around the city. 'Plain-living' puns on the plains.
explanation.definitionFit: A llanero is a herdsman of the South American plains, punning on a modest, simple life.

clue.text: Present lecture

definitions.meaning: to put forward or offer something for consideration
to speak at length in a preachy way

explanation.surface: Looks like a note saying a talk is to be given.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase once meant to offer or propose, and now means to talk at length on a subject.

clue.text: Part for actors in Othello and one in Twelfth Night

indicators.note: a part of the run of words gives the answer, sitting across the word boundaries

explanation.surface: A theatrical role for performers in two Shakespeare plays.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across actORS IN Othello. 'Part' looks like a stage role but signals a piece of the text.
explanation.definitionFit: Duke Orsino of Illyria is a character in Shakespeare's comedy, in love with Olivia.

clue.text: One way to eliminate wind and gas?

definitions.note: gas is informal for chatting idly

parts.note: to shoot someone is one way to eliminate them
a breeze is a light wind, here with the article

explanation.surface: A schoolboy joke about getting rid of flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' looks like the companion of 'wind' but is the definition: informal for chatting idly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to chat aimlessly, just as gassing is idle talk.

clue.text: It's facing west inside an old church, a centre of Christianity

indicators.note: the turned word goes into the letters that follow
in an across entry westward is leftward, so the word is turned back to front

parts.note: the word it, with the 's as a link

explanation.surface: Something points westward within an ancient church at a Christian hub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facing west' turns the word leftwards, as an across entry reads; 'inside' puts the turned pair within the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient city in present-day Turkey is where followers of Jesus were first called Christians.

clue.text: Authoritative statements, so clear when reinterpreted

indicators.note: reinterpreting gives the letters a new reading, a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pronouncements that seem plain once read a different way.
explanation.definitionFit: Oracles are prophetic utterances or pronouncements of unquestioned authority.

clue.text: Swimmer, one almost stuck in choppy Moselle

indicators.note: the shortened word is lodged inside the jumbled letters
choppy water is broken up, so the river's letters are broken and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as the word one

explanation.surface: A swimmer, apparently nearly alone, is stuck in a rough river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Choppy' scrambles the river into LEMSOLE; 'almost' trims one word; 'stuck in' lodges it inside. 'Swimmer' means a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimmer is crossword shorthand for a fish, and this is a flatfish.

clue.text: Mischievous fellow brought into line reformed

indicators.note: the fellow is placed inside the reworked letters
something reformed is made over in a new shape, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A troublemaker is brought into line and reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: LINE rearranged gives ELIN, with F inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves are impish sprites, so an impish, playful manner is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Draughtsmen proceed here, generally

definitions.meaning: draughtsmen are the pieces in draughts (checkers), which move over the playing surface
applying to everyone or everything without exception

explanation.surface: Seems to be about designers at work, broadly speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: Draughts is the British name for checkers; its pieces are draughtsmen, not drawing-office staff.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means applying universally to all cases, as a pay rise for everybody would.

clue.text: Romeo led astray by love initially, for example

indicators.note: letters led astray wander from their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Romeo misled by love is offered as an illustration.
explanation.definitionFit: A person held up as an example for others to copy is a figure worth imitating.

clue.text: One showing resentment about couple in partnership? Right

indicators.note: the resentment goes round the couple

parts.note: spite is malicious resentment
in bridge, North and South form one partnership

explanation.surface: Someone bitter about a married couple, and justifiably so?
explanation.walkthrough: The couple is North-South in bridge, not a married pair; 'about' wraps the resentment round them. 'One' is the definition in the sense of single, unwed.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried woman is single, and 'one' here stands for a single person.

clue.text: Store's entire management in disarray

definitions.meaning: read literally, being in charge of all the store

explanation.surface: A shop's whole board is in chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means scattered everywhere, disorganised and inconsistent.

clue.text: Shock tactics first used in the present epoch?

indicators.note: that letter is placed within the present epoch

parts.note: the present epoch is our age, the one we live in

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Asks whether shock tactics were first deployed in modern times.
explanation.walkthrough: T, the first letter of 'tactics', goes into OUR AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrage is a strong reaction of shock and indignation.

clue.text: Poet, say, is covered in English teaching

indicators.note: the pieces are wrapped inside the teaching abbreviation

parts.note: ELT stands for English Language Teaching
say introduces an example, as eg does

explanation.surface: A poet, for example, is covered in English classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covered in' wraps the teaching abbreviation round the rest; 'say' is not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegist is a writer of elegies, mournful verses, so a kind of versifier.

clue.text: Closer to target in battle over French waters?

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sits over, above, the other

parts.note: war is armed conflict
mer is French for sea

explanation.surface: Getting nearer the objective in a fight across French seas?
explanation.walkthrough: In hunting and guessing games, 'warmer' tells the seeker they are nearer the hidden object.
explanation.definitionFit: In children's guessing games a hotter word signals a searcher is nearing the hidden object.

clue.text: Accept modern male has to be with it

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks dates of the modern era

explanation.surface: Acknowledge that a contemporary man needs to be fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit something is to acknowledge or concede it, so to accept.

clue.text: African once travelled with Welsh girl astride horse

indicators.note: the travelling word sits astride the horse, around it

parts.note: rode means travelled on horseback
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
Sian is a Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: A former African went riding with a Welsh girl on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: RODE straddles H, then comes SIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodesia was the former name of Zimbabwe, so its citizens are Africans of an earlier era.

clue.text: Content of bride's trousseau, namely

indicators.note: the content of the words is letters held within them

explanation.surface: Looks like a list of what a bride packs for married life.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit in brIDE'S Trousseau.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase, usually written i.e., means that is to say.

clue.text: Beginning to intervene between me and girlfriend maybe do this?

definitions.text: Beginning to intervene between me and girlfriend maybe do this?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letter goes between the parts of the girlfriend word

parts.note: a date is someone you go out with, for example a girlfriend

indicators.note: the beginning of the next word gives its first letter

explanation.surface: Starting to step in between me and my partner, one would be doing this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Between' puts the letter inside the girlfriend word, not between the two words. The whole clue also describes the act.
explanation.definitionFit: Stepping in between two parties to settle a dispute is acting as a go-between.

clue.text: Distinguished artist associated with part of England (not the capital)

parts.note: Tracey Emin is a British artist

indicators.note: the capital here is the capital letter, the first one, which is dropped

parts.note: Kent is a county in south-east England

explanation.surface: A celebrated painter linked with a region outside London.
explanation.walkthrough: KENT loses its first, capital letter to give ENT. 'Capital' tempts you to London.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone eminent is notable and respected, standing out in their field.

clue.text: Thankful to be replaced

definitions.meaning: glad and grateful that a worry has passed
taken off duty when someone takes over the shift

explanation.surface: Grateful to be swapped out, like a worker at shift's end.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad that anxiety has lifted, and also freed from a post when a successor takes over.

clue.text: Old coin sister needed to enter London gallery

indicators.note: the gallery is entered into the sister's letters

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: An antique coin a nun had to bring into a London gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To enter' puts the gallery inside the sister's abbreviation, not the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: The stater was a gold or silver coin of ancient Greece.
